01-01: The euro is launched as the shared currency of 11 European Union countries.
01-02: Granada surrenders to Ferdinand and Isabella, ending the last Muslim kingdom in Spain.
01-03: Alaska becomes the 49th state of the United States.
01-05: Alexander Dubček takes over Czechoslovakia's Communist Party, opening the Prague Spring.
01-06: Harold Godwinson is crowned King of England, the last Anglo-Saxon king.
01-07: Galileo spots the moons of Jupiter through his telescope.
01-08: The Battle of New Orleans is fought, two weeks after the peace treaty ending the war was signed.
01-09: Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone.
01-10: The League of Nations comes into being as the Treaty of Versailles takes effect.
01-11: Insulin is given to a diabetic patient for the first time, in Toronto.
01-12: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake devastates Port-au-Prince, Haiti.
01-13: Émile Zola publishes "J'accuse…!", accusing the French army over the Dreyfus affair.
01-14: The US Congress ratifies the Treaty of Paris, formally ending the Revolutionary War.
01-16: The 18th Amendment is ratified, bringing Prohibition to the United States.
01-17: The air campaign of Operation Desert Storm begins against Iraq.
01-18: The German Empire is proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
01-19: Edgar Allan Poe is born in Boston.
01-20: John F. Kennedy is inaugurated: "Ask not what your country can do for you…"
01-21: King Louis XVI of France is executed by guillotine in Paris.
01-22: Queen Victoria dies after nearly 64 years on the throne.
01-23: The Shaanxi earthquake in China, the deadliest earthquake on record, strikes.
01-24: Gold is found at Sutter's Mill, setting off the California Gold Rush.
01-25: The first Winter Olympics open in Chamonix, France.
01-26: India's constitution takes effect and the country becomes a republic.
01-27: Soviet troops liberate the Auschwitz concentration camp.
01-28: The Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart shortly after launch.
01-29: Karl Benz patents his petrol-powered motor car.
01-30: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated in New Delhi.
01-31: Explorer 1, the first American satellite, is launched.
02-01: Ayatollah Khomeini returns to Iran from exile.
02-02: The last German forces surrender at Stalingrad.
02-03: The Soviet probe Luna 9 makes the first soft landing on the Moon.
02-04: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet at the Yalta Conference.
02-05: Apollo 14 lands on the Moon; Alan Shepard later hits golf balls there.
02-06: Māori chiefs and the British Crown sign the Treaty of Waitangi in New Zealand.
02-07: The Maastricht Treaty is signed; it creates the European Union the next year.
02-08: Mary, Queen of Scots is executed at Fotheringhay Castle.
02-09: The Beatles play on The Ed Sullivan Show to about 73 million viewers.
02-10: The Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War; France gives up Canada.
02-11: Nelson Mandela walks free after 27 years in prison.
02-12: Abraham Lincoln and Charles Darwin are born on the same day.
02-13: Allied bombers begin the raids that destroy much of Dresden.
02-14: Captain James Cook is killed in Hawaii.
02-15: Canada raises its red maple leaf flag for the first time.
02-16: Fidel Castro becomes Prime Minister of Cuba.
02-17: Philosopher Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake in Rome.
02-19: US Marines land on Iwo Jima.
02-20: John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit the Earth.
02-21: Marx and Engels publish The Communist Manifesto in London.
02-22: George Washington is born in Virginia.
02-23: US Marines raise the flag on Mount Suribachi, Iwo Jima.
02-24: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
02-25: Ferdinand Marcos flees the Philippines after the People Power Revolution.
02-26: Napoleon escapes from exile on Elba.
02-27: The Reichstag building in Berlin is set on fire.
02-28: Watson and Crick work out the double-helix structure of DNA.
02-29: Stranded in Jamaica, Columbus uses a predicted lunar eclipse to win supplies.
03-01: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park.
03-02: Texas declares its independence from Mexico.
03-03: Tsar Alexander II frees Russia's serfs.
03-04: Franklin Roosevelt is inaugurated: "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself."
03-05: Churchill warns of an "Iron Curtain" across Europe in a speech in Fulton, Missouri.
03-06: Ghana becomes the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence.
03-07: Alexander Graham Bell is granted a patent for the telephone.
03-08: Protests in Petrograd start the February Revolution in Russia.
03-09: The US Supreme Court frees the Africans who took over the slave ship Amistad.
03-10: An uprising against Chinese rule breaks out in Lhasa, Tibet.
03-11: An earthquake and tsunami strike Japan, causing the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
03-12: Gandhi begins the Salt March against British rule in India.
03-14: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm, Germany.
03-15: Julius Caesar is assassinated in Rome on the Ides of March.
03-16: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fuelled rocket.
03-17: White South Africans vote in a referendum to end apartheid.
03-18: The Paris Commune takes power in the French capital.
03-21: South African police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville.
03-22: The Arab League is founded in Cairo.
03-23: Patrick Henry declares "Give me liberty, or give me death!"
03-24: Elizabeth I dies; James VI of Scotland becomes King of England too.
03-25: The Treaty of Rome is signed, founding the European Economic Community.
03-27: The Great Alaska earthquake, the strongest recorded in North America, strikes.
03-28: A partial meltdown occurs at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant.
03-29: The last US combat troops leave South Vietnam.
03-30: The United States agrees to buy Alaska from Russia.
03-31: The Eiffel Tower is inaugurated in Paris.
04-01: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne found Apple.
04-03: Martin Cooper makes the first call from a handheld mobile phone.
04-04: Twelve countries sign the North Atlantic Treaty, founding NATO.
04-05: Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen reaches Easter Island on Easter Sunday.
04-06: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens.
04-07: The genocide against the Tutsi begins in Rwanda.
04-08: The Venus de Milo is found on the Greek island of Milos.
04-09: Robert E. Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House.
04-10: The Good Friday Agreement is signed, a turning point for peace in Northern Ireland.
04-11: Napoleon abdicates under the Treaty of Fontainebleau.
04-12: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space.
04-13: British troops fire on a crowd at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar.
04-14: Abraham Lincoln is shot at Ford's Theatre.
04-15: The Titanic sinks after hitting an iceberg.
04-16: The Battle of Culloden ends the last Jacobite rising.
04-17: The Bay of Pigs invasion of Cuba begins.
04-18: An earthquake and fire destroy much of San Francisco.
04-19: The battles of Lexington and Concord start the American Revolutionary War.
04-20: The Deepwater Horizon oil rig explodes in the Gulf of Mexico.
04-21: The traditional date of the founding of Rome by Romulus.
04-22: The first Earth Day is held.
04-24: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched.
04-25: The Carnation Revolution topples Portugal's dictatorship.
04-26: A reactor explodes at the Chernobyl nuclear plant.
04-27: South Africa holds its first election open to all races.
04-29: US troops liberate the Dachau concentration camp.
04-30: Saigon falls to North Vietnamese forces.
05-01: The Great Exhibition opens in London's Crystal Palace.
05-02: Berlin surrenders to the Soviet Red Army.
05-03: Poland adopts Europe's first modern written constitution.
05-04: Student protests in Beijing launch the May Fourth Movement.
05-05: Napoleon dies in exile on Saint Helena.
05-06: Roger Bannister runs the first mile under four minutes.
05-07: A German U-boat sinks the liner Lusitania.
05-08: Victory in Europe Day: Germany's surrender takes effect.
05-09: The Schuman Declaration proposes pooling French and German coal and steel.
05-10: Nelson Mandela is inaugurated as South Africa's first Black president.
05-11: IBM's Deep Blue beats world chess champion Garry Kasparov.
05-12: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake strikes Sichuan, China.
05-13: Pope John Paul II is shot and wounded in St Peter's Square.
05-14: David Ben-Gurion declares the State of Israel.
05-15: The Austrian State Treaty is signed, ending the Allied occupation of Austria.
05-16: The first Academy Awards are presented in Hollywood.
05-17: The US Supreme Court rules school segregation unconstitutional in Brown v. Board.
05-18: Mount St. Helens erupts in Washington State.
05-19: Anne Boleyn is executed at the Tower of London.
05-20: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, India, by sea from Portugal.
05-21: Charles Lindbergh lands in Paris after the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight.
05-23: West Germany's Basic Law is signed, founding the Federal Republic.
05-24: Samuel Morse sends the telegraph message "What hath God wrought".
05-25: The Organisation of African Unity is founded in Addis Ababa.
05-26: Nicholas II is crowned, the last Tsar of Russia.
05-28: Mathias Rust, 19, flies a small plane from Finland and lands near Red Square.
05-29: Constantinople falls to the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II.
05-30: Joan of Arc is burned at the stake in Rouen.
05-31: The Treaty of Vereeniging ends the Second Boer War.
06-01: CNN, the first 24-hour news channel, goes on air.
06-02: Elizabeth II is crowned at Westminster Abbey.
06-03: Ed White makes the first American spacewalk.
06-04: Troops crush protests in Tiananmen Square as Solidarity sweeps Poland's elections.
06-05: George Marshall proposes the Marshall Plan to rebuild Europe.
06-06: D-Day: Allied forces land in Normandy.
06-07: Spain and Portugal divide the world outside Europe in the Treaty of Tordesillas.
06-08: George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four is published.
06-09: The Final Act of the Congress of Vienna is signed.
06-10: Italy declares war on France and Britain.
06-11: President Kennedy tells the nation civil rights are "a moral issue".
06-12: Ronald Reagan in Berlin: "Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!"
06-13: The first V-1 flying bombs hit London.
06-14: The US Congress adopts the Stars and Stripes as the national flag.
06-15: King John seals Magna Carta at Runnymede.
06-16: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space.
06-17: Burglars are arrested inside the Watergate complex.
06-19: Enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, learn they are free: Juneteenth.
06-20: French deputies swear the Tennis Court Oath.
06-21: The Manchester Baby runs the first program stored in a computer's memory.
06-22: Germany invades the Soviet Union in Operation Barbarossa.
06-23: Alan Turing is born in London.
06-24: The Soviet Union blockades West Berlin; the Berlin Airlift follows.
06-26: The United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco.
06-27: The world's first nuclear power plant feeds a grid, at Obninsk, USSR.
06-28: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is shot in Sarajevo; five years later the Treaty of Versailles is signed.
06-29: The Globe Theatre in London burns down during a Shakespeare play.
06-30: A huge explosion flattens 2,000 km² of Siberian forest at Tunguska.
07-01: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China.
07-02: President Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act.
07-04: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence.
07-05: Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, is born.
07-06: Louis Pasteur first gives his rabies vaccine to a boy, who survives.
07-07: The Marco Polo Bridge Incident starts full war between China and Japan.
07-08: Commodore Perry's warships arrive in Edo Bay to open Japan.
07-09: South Sudan becomes independent, the world's newest country.
07-11: The Srebrenica massacre begins in Bosnia.
07-12: Napoleon creates the Confederation of the Rhine.
07-13: The Live Aid concerts are held in London and Philadelphia.
07-14: Crowds storm the Bastille in Paris.
07-15: French soldiers find the Rosetta Stone in Egypt.
07-16: The first atomic bomb is tested in New Mexico.
07-17: Truman, Churchill and Stalin open the Potsdam Conference.
07-19: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out.
07-21: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, a Wonder of the World, is burned down.
07-22: The Bretton Woods conference ends, creating the IMF and the World Bank.
07-23: The Free Officers overthrow Egypt's King Farouk.
07-25: Louise Brown, the first IVF baby, is born.
07-27: The Korean War armistice is signed.
07-29: Eisenhower signs the law creating NASA.
07-30: England wins the football World Cup at Wembley.
07-31: The US and the USSR sign START I to cut nuclear arsenals.
08-01: Three Alpine cantons swear the alliance that founds Switzerland (traditional date).
08-03: Columbus sets sail from Palos, Spain.
08-05: The US, UK and USSR sign the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.
08-06: The United States drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima.
08-07: Thor Heyerdahl's raft Kon-Tiki reaches Polynesia from Peru.
08-09: Singapore separates from Malaysia and becomes independent.
08-10: Paris crowds storm the Tuileries Palace, toppling the French monarchy.
08-11: The start date of the Maya Long Count calendar (most common correlation).
08-13: East Germany begins building the Berlin Wall.
08-18: During a solar eclipse, astronomers see the spectral line later named helium.
08-19: Hardliners attempt a coup against Gorbachev in Moscow.
08-21: The Mona Lisa is stolen from the Louvre.
08-22: The first Geneva Convention is signed.
08-23: Germany and the USSR sign the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact.
08-24: Mount Vesuvius erupts, burying Pompeii (traditional date).
08-26: France adopts the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
08-28: Martin Luther King Jr. gives his "I Have a Dream" speech.
08-29: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb.
08-30: The Moscow-Washington hotline goes into operation.
08-31: The Gdańsk Agreement allows Poland's Solidarity union.
09-01: Germany invades Poland, starting World War II in Europe.
09-02: Japan formally surrenders; Ho Chi Minh declares Vietnam's independence.
09-03: The Treaty of Paris recognises the independence of the United States.
09-04: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last Western Roman emperor.
09-05: The Treaty of Portsmouth ends the Russo-Japanese War.
09-06: Magellan's ship Victoria returns to Spain, completing the first voyage around the world.
09-08: The Treaty of San Francisco is signed, ending the Allied occupation of Japan.
09-09: Congress renames the "United Colonies" the "United States".
09-10: The Large Hadron Collider circulates its first proton beam.
09-11: Terrorist attacks hit New York and Washington.
09-12: Teenagers discover the prehistoric cave paintings of Lascaux.
09-13: Israel and the PLO sign the Oslo Accords at the White House.
09-15: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens.
09-16: The Mayflower sails from Plymouth, England.
09-17: The US Constitution is signed in Philadelphia.
09-18: The Mukden Incident gives Japan its pretext to invade Manchuria.
09-19: New Zealand becomes the first country where women can vote in national elections.
09-21: J.R.R. Tolkien's The Hobbit is published.
09-22: Lincoln issues the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation.
09-23: Astronomers find Neptune where mathematics predicted it.
09-24: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty opens for signature.
09-25: Balboa becomes the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas.
09-26: Kennedy and Nixon hold the first televised presidential debate.
09-27: The first Ford Model T is built.
09-28: Alexander Fleming notices penicillin killing bacteria.
09-30: The Munich Agreement hands Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland to Germany.
10-01: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China.
10-04: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite.
10-05: The women's march on Versailles forces the French royal family to Paris.
10-06: Egypt and Syria attack Israel, starting the Yom Kippur War.
10-07: A Holy League fleet defeats the Ottomans at Lepanto.
10-08: The Great Chicago Fire breaks out.
10-09: Che Guevara is executed in Bolivia.
10-10: The Wuchang Uprising begins the revolution that ends imperial China.
10-12: Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas.
10-13: King Philip IV of France has the Knights Templar arrested.
10-14: William of Normandy wins the Battle of Hastings.
10-15: The Gregorian calendar starts: in Catholic countries, 4 October is followed by 15 October.
10-16: Kennedy is shown photos of Soviet missiles in Cuba: the Cuban Missile Crisis begins.
10-17: Arab oil producers announce the oil embargo.
10-18: The British Broadcasting Company, later the BBC, is founded.
10-20: Queen Elizabeth II opens the Sydney Opera House.
10-21: Nelson defeats the French and Spanish fleets at Trafalgar.
10-22: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute jump, over Paris.
10-23: The Hungarian Revolution begins in Budapest.
10-24: The United Nations officially comes into existence.
10-25: Henry V's English army wins at Agincourt.
10-26: The Football Association is founded in London.
10-28: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated.
10-29: Mustafa Kemal proclaims the Republic of Turkey.
10-30: Orson Welles's radio play The War of the Worlds alarms listeners.
10-31: Martin Luther's 95 Theses start the Protestant Reformation.
11-01: The Maastricht Treaty takes effect and the European Union is born.
11-03: The dog Laika becomes the first animal to orbit the Earth.
11-04: Howard Carter's team finds the first step to Tutankhamun's tomb.
11-05: The Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament is foiled.
11-07: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd (the October Revolution).
11-10: Henry Morton Stanley finds David Livingstone: "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"
11-11: The Armistice ends the fighting of World War I at 11 a.m.
11-12: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web at CERN.
11-13: Paul Cornu makes the first free flight of a helicopter.
11-14: Mariner 9 becomes the first spacecraft to orbit another planet, Mars.
11-15: The League of Nations holds its first Assembly in Geneva.
11-20: The Nuremberg trials of Nazi leaders begin.
11-21: Two men make the first free flight in a hot-air balloon, over Paris.
11-22: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas.
11-23: Doctor Who is first broadcast on the BBC.
11-24: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species.
11-25: Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity.
11-27: Pope Urban II calls for the First Crusade.
11-28: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet at the Tehran Conference.
11-29: The UN General Assembly votes to partition Palestine.
11-30: Scotland and England play the first international football match.
12-01: Twelve countries sign the Antarctic Treaty.
12-02: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French.
12-03: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant in Cape Town.
12-04: The ship Mary Celeste is found drifting with no one on board.
12-05: Prohibition ends in the United States.
12-08: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agree to dissolve the Soviet Union.
12-09: The UN adopts the Genocide Convention.
12-10: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
12-12: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal.
12-13: Abel Tasman becomes the first European to sight New Zealand.
12-14: Roald Amundsen's team reaches the South Pole.
12-15: The US Bill of Rights is ratified.
12-16: Colonists dump British tea into the harbour: the Boston Tea Party.
12-17: The Wright brothers make the first powered aeroplane flights.
12-18: The 13th Amendment abolishing slavery takes effect in the United States.
12-19: Britain and China sign the Joint Declaration on Hong Kong's future.
12-20: France hands Louisiana to the United States in New Orleans.
12-21: Apollo 8 launches, the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
12-22: The Brandenburg Gate reopens in Berlin.
12-23: Bell Labs demonstrates the first transistor.
12-24: Soldiers on the Western Front hold an unofficial Christmas truce.
12-25: Charlemagne is crowned emperor in Rome.
12-27: Charles Darwin sails from Plymouth aboard HMS Beagle.
12-28: The Lumière brothers hold the first public film screening, in Paris.
12-29: Archbishop Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral.
12-31: Elizabeth I charters the East India Company.
